messages:
marie: quick thought — proposing a temporary 'tap' mode in the console to route full request+response payloads for short-lived debug sessions on canaries. need guardrails for sampling, PII, and quota.
leo: +1 for a controlled tap. main concerns: cost, accidental enablement, and how we redact PII.
anna: console UX question — should tap be per-route or per-deployment? per-route seems safer but more config.
jordan: legal: if we capture full payloads we must enforce PII redaction AND an approval audit trail. can't have engineers toggling this without oversight.
marie: agreed. my thinking: per-route tap with TTL (e.g., 15m), max_samples cap, tenant-scoped, and a recorded justification required at enable. UI shows who enabled and when.
leo: technical constraints — caching and batching mean we might not get exact req/res pairs if we sample post-batch. need synchronous passthrough for tapped requests or tag before batching.
mike: can we do a mode where tapped requests are routed to a non-batched path? that'll hit latency but only for a small percentage.
anna: UX: make the console show an estimated cost before enabling (approx tokens, GPU secs). add a big red warning about PII.
marie: policy idea: tap requires either (a) a legal/infra approve toggle for tenants marked 'sensitive' OR (b) 2fa enable + reason for standard tenants. also auto-disable after TTL.
jordan: add full HMAC fingerprinting of any fields we drop so we can correlate without storing raw PII. also keep short retention logs of approvals.
leo: redact approach — pipeline should first apply deid heuristics (email/ssn/creditcard regex), then fast-hash HMAC fields customer-marked as sensitive, then optionally keep tokenized placeholder. fallback: if heuristics uncertain, disallow tap and require manual review.
srebot: deploy note: last time someone enabled debug-tap we saw a 3x spike in storage. tagging as FYI.
audit-bot: ACTION logged: marie requested design thread for console tap. Please add proposed schema to #design when ready.
mike: small config sketch: ```yaml
tap:
  enabled: true
  scope: route
  ttl: 15m
  max_samples: 200
  synchronous_passthrough: true
  pii_scrub: auto
  approval_required: true
```
anna: question on telemetry: how do we count these in usage billing? as normal tokens or separate debug tokens? ops: we should surface them separately so they don't skew model cost metrics used for billing.
leo: also need rate caps per-tenant so tap can't starve dedicated pools. recommend per-tenant concurrent_tap limit and a global tap budget.
jordan: legal: retention for raw tapped payloads must be <30d and access must go through an audited UI. also add opt-out flag for customers.
marie: implementation plan: (1) console flag + enable flow (2) runtime route tagging + synchronous path (3) server-side scrub/hmac step pre-persist (4) approval audit + TTL enforcement (5) telemetry counters in console + separate billing metric.
mike: for runtime tagging: add header X-Redwood-Tap: <session-id>. runtime will short-circuit batching if header present.
leo: fallback for third-party SDKs: SDKs send Tap header but if absent, console can proxy via our inspect-proxy; costlier but works.
anna: small mockup: show 'Start Tap' modal with dropdown for route, TTL slider, max samples, reason text box, and checkbox "I understand this may include PII".
jordan: legal wants a checkbox with link to data handling policy + email alert to tenant admins when tap enabled.
marie: ops/infra question — do we need a separate storage tier for tapped data (encrypted, short TTL)? probably yes. thoughts?
srebot: yes separate bucket with KMS key and limited read ACL. automatic lifecycle rule to delete after TTL.
leo: technical risk: if tap goes to non-batched path we may bypass certain optimizations (kv cache). acceptable for short TTL but we need to track correctness for metrics. add integration test for KV cache parity.
mike: dev-api change: internal endpoint /v1/debug/tap will return a signed session id and route config. console will POST to that to start session.
anna: anything else on UX? also show a "recent taps" list per-route with who enabled and reason, plus quick revoke.
jordan: thumbs up if we attach the approval log to the audit trail so compliance can query.
marie: ok I'll draft a short RFC with config schema, console mockups, and runtime flow. will include redaction heuristics and HMAC approach. pinging @jordan @leo for review before I send to #design.
leo: will review. also propose a small canary: enable tap only on staging initially for 2 weeks, then open limited beta.
nana: (typo) — wanna say +1 on staged rollouts.
marie: thanks all. saving notes here. future TODOs: sample retention TTL, per-tenant budget UI, billing metric, infra bucket + KMS, SDK header docs.
